item.title: Grammys Open Black History Month as Michael Jackson’s Story Heads to the Big Screen
item.description: Sunday’s Grammy Awards opened Black History Month while also setting the tone for a year that will once again bring Michael Jackson to the forefront of popular culture.

item.title: Don Lemon Made the Headlines, but Georgia Fort’s Arrest Shows No Journalist Is Safe
item.description: Fort documented her own arrest in a brief livestream as agents arrived at her door, telling viewers she was being taken into custody for filming the protest as a member of the press.

item.title: History Will Remember Who Spoke and Who Hid
item.description: Journalists were arrested for doing their jobs. Not in some distant dictatorship. Not under cover of night in a failed state. In the United States of America.

item.title: Demond Wilson, Who Played Lamont on ‘Sanford and Son,’ Dies at 79
item.description: Demond Wilson, who found fame in the 1970s playing Lamont on “Sanford and Son” and went on to become a minister, has died. He was 79.

item.title: After Don Lemon’s Arrest, Black Officials Raise Concerns About Independent Black Media
item.description: The implications of Fort’s and Lemon’s arrests have drawn responses from leaders of the California Legislative Black Caucus (CLBC) who were not on the Zoom call.
